author: blu
body: Every other constructor of a TcpTransportState in TcpTransport carries the three fields. This one is the exception, and it was the exception by omission rather than by intent.

author: blu
body: A plug answers in target-language source, which is Text, and this is the send it wants. It was missing here, so all 41 transpiler plugs carried their own byte-identical `send-text-loop` -- shadowing the transport rather than a missing cite, since every one of them already cites this chapter. Each copy also re-spelled `TcpTransportState`'s seven-field literal, which is how one incomplete literal became 46 bugs and how `net-io-send-chunk` above came to drop three fields and write inbound frames to physical address zero.

author: blu
body: Only the send half moves here. The receive half (`bytes-to-text-chunk`) stays in the plugs, because it is NOT the same function in all of them: 40 accumulate into a `Text`, and `CSharpPlug` accumulates into a `List Text`. Same name, two types, and hoisting one of them would have quietly given the other a different function -- which is the duplicate-name hazard, met here in miniature.

author: blu
body: A MESSAGE ALREADY IN THE BUFFER IS ANSWERED WITHOUT WAITING FOR A FRAME, and without this the message is simply lost. `transport-process-frame` feeds a segment's payload into the receive buffer and tries to take a message out of it, so a complete message can be sitting there before anyone asks. The wait loop below blocks on `net-driver-recv-frame` first, so it would sit waiting for a frame that has already been and gone.

author: blu
body: It happens on the ordinary path, not a rare one. A client's final handshake ACK usually carries its first request piggybacked (PSH+ACK), so ONE frame both establishes the connection and delivers the request. `net-io-accept` returns the moment the connection is established and looks at nothing else, so the request rides in on the frame that ends the handshake and is buffered; the server then calls this and waits forever for a request it is already holding.

author: blu
body: Measured on `tools/cdx-registry`: it served its first request, went back to accept, took the second connection, and sat in this loop with the second request already buffered.
